q: A ramp worker in a transportation practicum puts on a hi-vis vest, checks that her hearing protection fits and walks around the aircraft tug before starting it. She is:
o: understanding and applying proper safety techniques in the workplace

q: Why do trained workers follow safety techniques even on routine jobs?
o: Most accidents happen when routine steps are skipped
Safety is only for new hires

q: During a shift handoff, a dispatcher gives the next person a short, clear summary and points to the map to show the delay. She is:
o: using verbal and non-verbal communication in a clear, concise and effective manner

q: Which message to a crew is the clearest and most concise?
o: "Um, you know, that truck thing, sometime later maybe."
"Somebody should probably do something at the docks."
"Truck 4 loads at Dock B by 2:00 p.m."

q: A trainee reads a fuel-use chart for three delivery routes, explains which route costs most and gives the numbers to her supervisor. She is:
o: analyzing, interpreting and communicating data and observations effectively

q: When reporting data to a supervisor, a worker should:
o: state what the numbers show and what they mean

q: A trainee sees her supervisor's furrowed brow while she explains a delay and slows down to ask if more detail would help. She is:
o: observing and interpreting nonverbal cues to improve communication

q: A customer says 'fine' but crosses her arms and looks away. A skilled worker would:
o: ask a follow-up question to find out what is wrong

q: A trainee repeats a pickup address back to the caller and asks, 'Is that the north entrance?' before dispatching a driver. She is:
o: applying active listening to obtain and clarify information

q: Which habit is part of active listening?
o: Planning your answer while the speaker talks
Asking questions to confirm what was said

q: A trainee's cart will not start, so she checks the battery, then the cable, then the switch, using each result to decide what to test next. She is:
o: employing critical-thinking skills independently with increased fluency

q: Critical thinking at work means a person:
A warehouse crew keeps blocking an aisle, so a trainee proposes painting loading zones and changing the pickup order. She is:
o: analyzing elements of a problem to develop creative and innovative solutions

q: Before offering a creative fix, a worker should first:
o: identify the parts and the cause of the problem

q: A trainee tells a customer that the part has a worn bearing and needs a torque check, using the terms her program taught. She is:
o: using content, technical concepts and vocabulary when analyzing information

q: Why is accurate technical vocabulary valuable on a job site?
o: It prevents misunderstandings that cause errors

q: A trainee follows posted workplace rules about lockout of equipment and wears the required gear before servicing a conveyor. She is:
o: consistently following workplace safety rules and regulations

q: Following safety rules is most important:
o: every time a task is performed

q: A trainee knows to stop work, tell her supervisor and fill out the incident form when a coworker is hurt by a loose pallet. She is:
o: demonstrating knowledge of procedures for reporting and handling accidents and safety incidents

q: Why must workers report every accident, even a small one?
o: Reports help prevent the same accident from happening again

q: A trainee finishes each assigned task as directed, stays busy when work is slow and keeps a good attitude. She is:
o: demonstrating a positive, productive work ethic by performing assigned tasks as directed

q: A supervisor is away for the afternoon and a junior worker still stacks every pallet and cleans the bay. What does this show?
A coworker asks a trainee to round up the hours on a shared log sheet, and she declines after considering what is fair and honest. She is:
o: applying ethical reasoning to make an ethical decision

q: An ethical decision at work is one that is:
o: honest and fair to everyone affected

q: A trainee checks that her driving hours and her paperwork follow all the laws and company rules before a trip. She is:
o: complying with all applicable rules, laws and regulations in a consistent manner

q: Why do transportation workers have to follow laws and regulations?
o: They protect the safety of workers and the public

q: A trainee in a supervised practicum carries out a service task, writes up what she did and reviews how it went with her mentor. She is:
o: conducting, documenting and evaluating learning activities in a supervised transportation setting

q: Documenting a learning activity helps a student because it:
o: creates a record she can review and improve from

q: A trainee practices a new brake inspection method under supervision to move beyond basic skills for her chosen occupation. She is:
o: developing advanced technical knowledge and skills related to her occupational objective

q: Advanced skills in an occupation are usually built by:
o: repeated practice with feedback from experts

q: A trainee's logbook shows she now completes a tire service in half the time with fewer errors than in the fall. She is:
o: demonstrating growth of technical skill competencies

q: A good way to show skill growth over time is to:
A trainee reviews her checklist and notes that she is strong at inspections but needs practice on documentation. She is:
o: evaluating strengths and weaknesses in technical skill proficiency

q: Knowing a weakness in a skill allows a student to:
o: plan practice where it is needed most

q: A trainee saves a photo of a finished repair, a completed inspection form and a supervisor's note in a folder. She is:
A representative work sample should:
o: show typical, quality work from the student
